required_corrections.target: current_source_findings F4 fact and consequence; legacy cancellation summaries
required_corrections.reason: The current flag/termination attempt does not prove the reader unblocked or child exited. Existing cleanup deliberately retains an uncertain child.
required_corrections.replacement_fact: Cancel marks the tracked child as stopped-by-spaCR and requests terminate; it bounded-waits and requests kill only after a termination wait timeout. Signal/wait errors are swallowed. StreamWorker.cancel sets a local flag and calls the provider; it emits no finished signal. run reports Cancelled only after iteration or exception handling regains control. If the stdout read stays blocked and termination fails, completion may remain pending. _stream_process cleanup removes handles only when exit is confirmed; an uncertain child stays on the provider and in _LIVE_STREAMS for later shutdown retry.
required_corrections.replacement_consequence: Cancel requested, a stopped marker and local worker state do not prove transport termination. Even a confirmed direct-child exit is not vendor turn/tool acknowledgement, descendant cessation or rollback. Do not show confirmed cancellation solely from the flag or a terminate request; preserve findable uncertain children and distinguish worker completion, child exit and provider terminal evidence.

required_corrections.target: platform qualification beside claude-print-no-host cancellation and shared cancellation boundary
required_corrections.reason: SIGTERM semantics apply to POSIX signaling, whereas current Windows Popen termination uses TerminateProcess. Vendor documentation is not universal descendant proof.
required_corrections.replacement_qualification: On POSIX, the current Popen.terminate call sends SIGTERM and timeout escalation requests SIGKILL; on Windows, terminate invokes TerminateProcess and kill aliases it. Claude documented SIGTERM turn/prompt/Bash-child cleanup is current signal-specific vendor documentation, not installed-release, Windows or universal descendant acceptance. SDK interrupt/close are distinct protocol/lifecycle operations. Confirm any future adapter per supported OS/build; no such runtime acceptance is delivered here.
